stem: A team must choose EC2 configurations for two separate needs: an application requiring genuinely isolated hardware for a small number of critical instances in one Availability Zone, and a large HDFS cluster that must contain any single rack failure to a limited blast radius. Which TWO placement group types fit? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: EFA enabled without any placement group
Graviton instances placed in a single partition placement group

rationale: A spread placement group places a small number of critical instances each on genuinely distinct hardware within an Availability Zone, matching the requirement for isolated hardware for a few critical instances. A partition placement group divides instances into partitions on separate racks with independent power and networking, containing a single hardware failure to one partition, which matches the HDFS cluster's blast-radius requirement. A cluster placement group packs instances together on the same network segment for the lowest latency, the opposite of the hardware isolation both scenarios call for. EFA adds a low-latency transport for HPC workloads; it does not by itself provide hardware isolation or failure-domain containment without a placement group. Putting Graviton instances in a single partition still concentrates them in one partition, so it does not contain a rack failure to a limited blast radius the way spreading across multiple partitions does.
